about: The epistola of the formulary “10th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: You know that when you were Gentiles, it was to mute idols that you went, just as you were being led. Therefore I make known to you that no one who speaks in the Spirit of God pronounces anathema on Jesus. Nor can anyone say: Jesus is Lord, except in the Holy Spirit. There are, however, distributions of graces, but the same Spirit. There are also distributions of services, but the same Lord; there are also distributions of operations, but the same God, who accomplishes all things in all. And to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for what is useful. To one the word of wisdom is given through the Spirit; to another the word of knowledge, in keeping with the same Spirit; to yet another faith, in that same Spirit; to another the grace of healings, in one Spirit; to another the performing of mighty works; to another prophecy; to another discernment of spirits; to another varieties of tongues; to another the interpretation of utterances. But one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each one as He wills.
